info.title: Geo API
info.description:
Find the coordinates of an address or a place, and calculate a route between two points.

The Geo API is a read-only API with two resources:

* [`GET /coordinates`](./geo-api.json/paths/~1coordinates/get) turns free text (an address, a venue, a point of interest) into coordinates.
* [`GET /routes`](./geo-api.json/paths/~1routes/get) calculates a route between an origin and a destination, each given as coordinates or as free text.

Read the [introduction](../docs/introduction.md) and the guides before you start.

Authentication is not part of this version of the contract yet; it will be added in a later version.

LocationCollection.title: locationCollection
LocationCollection.description: The locations that matched a query, best match first.

totalItems.description: Number of locations in `member`, at most `limit`. `0` when nothing matched. The collection is not paginated.

member.description: The matching locations, best match first.

RouteCollection.title: routeCollection
RouteCollection.description: The calculated route(s) and the waypoints they run through.

totalItems.description: Number of routes in `member`: `1`, plus the number of alternatives that could be found. The collection is not paginated.

member.description: The recommended route first, then the alternatives if requested.

waypoints.description: The origin, the via points in order, and the destination, as coordinates, as the API resolved them. Check these when you passed text instead of coordinates.

query.name: query
query.description: The text to find coordinates for: an address (`Sint-Pietersplein 1, Gent`), a venue or point of interest (`Vooruit Gent`), or just a municipality (`Gent`). Add the municipality for better results.

country.name: country
country.description: Only return locations in this country. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.

limit.name: limit
limit.description: Maximum number of locations to return. Results are ordered best match first, so the default of 1 gives you the best match. This collection is not paginated: `totalItems` is the number of returned locations.

origin.name: origin
origin.description: Where the route starts. Either coordinates as `latitude,longitude` in decimal degrees, or free text that is resolved like the `query` parameter of `GET /coordinates` (the best match is used). See [calculating routes](../docs/calculating-routes.md#coordinates-or-text).

destination.name: destination
destination.description: Where the route ends. Same format as `origin`.

via.name: via
via.description: Points the route must pass through, in order. Same format as `origin`. Repeat the parameter for several points: `?via=51.05,3.72&via=51.04,3.73`. Cannot be combined with `alternatives`.

geometry.name: geometry
geometry.description: Format of the route shape in the response: an encoded polyline (precision 6), a GeoJSON LineString, or no shape at all.

alternatives.name: alternatives
alternatives.description: Number of alternative routes to return next to the recommended one. Fewer may be returned when no sensible alternatives exist. Cannot be combined with `via` or `departAt`.

departAt.name: departAt
departAt.description: Departure date and time, ISO 8601 with an offset or `Z`, for time-dependent restrictions such as roads closed at certain hours. The instant is converted to local time at the origin. Defaults to no time dependency. Cannot be combined with `alternatives`.

boundsPadding.name: boundsPadding
boundsPadding.description: Metres added to every side of the route extent to produce `bounds`. `0` (the default) gives the exact extent of the route; pass a few hundred metres to search for events within walking distance of the route.

routeCountry.name: country
routeCountry.description: Country used to resolve `origin`, `destination` and `via` when they are given as text. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Has no effect on points given as coordinates, and does not restrict the route itself: a route may cross a border.

NotFound.description:
The requested resource (URL) could not be found. This can be due to one of multiple reasons:

* The endpoint has a typo and/or does not exist on the API
* One of the required query parameters is missing
* One of the query parameters has an invalid value

The `detail` property of the response contains more specific information.

The `type` is always `https://api.publiq.be/probs/url/not-found`.

RouteNotFound.description:
The requested resource (URL) could not be found. Next to the generic reasons (a required query parameter is missing or has an invalid value, `type` `https://api.publiq.be/probs/url/not-found`), this operation has two domain-specific reasons. See the [errors page](../docs/errors.md) for details.

* `https://api.publiq.be/probs/geo-api/location-not-found`: `origin`, `destination` or a `via` point was given as text and no location matched it
* `https://api.publiq.be/probs/geo-api/route-not-found`: all points were resolved but no route exists between them for the given `mode`

The `detail` property of the response contains more specific information.

value.title: Not Found
value.detail: Query parameter "alternatives" cannot be combined with "via"

value.title: Route not found
value.detail: No pedestrian route exists between the origin and the destination

BadGateway.description:
One of the sources the Geo API depends on did not answer or answered with an error. Retry the request after a short delay. If the problem persists, contact the publiq helpdesk.

* type: about:blank
* title: Bad Gateway

get.description:
Returns the locations that match a free-text `query`, best match first, as coordinates.

The query can be an address, a venue or point of interest, or just a municipality. The API looks the text up in several sources in a fixed order and returns the results of the first source that knows it: places in UiTdatabank first, then an address database.

A query that matches nothing returns `200` with an empty `member`, not an error.

Read the [finding coordinates](../docs/finding-coordinates.md) guide for tips.

200.description: The matching locations, best match first. An empty `member` means nothing matched.

get.description:
Returns the recommended route between `origin` and `destination` (through the `via` points, in order), and up to three `alternatives` when asked.

Each point is either `latitude,longitude` or free text. Text is resolved the same way as [`GET /coordinates`](./geo-api.json/paths/~1coordinates/get) and the best match is used; the `waypoints` in the response show what was used, so you can check it.

Every route comes with `bounds`: its extent plus `boundsPadding` metres on every side, ready to pass to the `bounds` filter of UiTdatabank's Search API to find events along the way. Read the [calculating routes](../docs/calculating-routes.md) guide for that flow.

200.description: The recommended route first, then the alternatives if any, plus the resolved waypoints.
